films.lineage: Lineage: Everynone, Symmetry (2011), commissioned with WNYC Radiolab

films.title: Losers — Social Position Through Montage
films.subtitle: How apparent difficulty changes when surrounding conduct becomes visible
films.lineage: Lineage: Everynone / Daniel Mercadante, Losers
films.theorem: Show how a person's apparent social position changes when the surrounding responses become visible. Make the audience reconsider a label through observable conduct rather than invented motives.
films.boundary_note: Constructed from coherent multi-person table recordings (`Working Together`, 1951 and `How Quiet Helps at School`, 1953) by comparing tight isolation crops against wide room geometry of the exact same scene.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #02 (t=03.50s-09.00s): `e5aa6366` shows an animated cartoon character (`Just Imagine`, 1947) instead of a tight view of a person at a shared table.
Seg #03-#06 (t=09.00s-32.00s): Unrelated rooms across decades prevent re-contextualizing the same person's social position through framing.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: Instead of revealing how widening the frame changes the interpretation of the same person's difficulty at a shared table, v1 spliced an animated cartoon with unrelated rooms.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: Independent clip retrieval per beat label instead of extracting tight-cropped and wide-context views from a coherent multi-person table recording.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Use the new `reframe` operator (`tight` -> `tight_to_wide` -> `wide`) on verified continuous multi-person table recordings `79565922` (`Working Together`, 1951, 10.0s-28.4s) and `98a82cba` (`How Quiet Helps at School`, 1953, 0.5s-21.0s), then reverse the order (`wide` -> `tight`) in the Comparison Cut after the slate.
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: The rhetorical structure of the Wide-First Comparison Cut slate (Seg #07) and the quiet unresolved workroom atmosphere.
